title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 218
paragraphs: While the Persians were climbing, they were hidden from the Phokians because the whole mountain was covered with oak trees. The Phokians became aware of them after they had completed the ascent, in this way: the day was still, and the Persians made no small noise — as was natural when leaves lay strewn on the ground under their feet. At that, the Phokians sprang up and began to put on their armor, and by this time the barbarians were close at hand. The barbarians, when they saw men arming themselves, were astonished, for they had expected no one to appear to oppose them, and instead they had encountered an armed force. Hydarnes, seized with fear that the Phokians might be Lacedaemonians, asked Epialtes what people this force belonged to; and when he had been accurately informed, he drew up the Persians for battle. The Phokians, when the enemy's arrows came thick upon them, fled at once to the topmost peak of the mountain, convinced that it was against them that the enemy had come, and there they prepared to meet their death. So they, at least, were in this frame of mind. Meanwhile the Persians under Epialtes and Hydarnes paid no attention to the Phokians, but descended the mountain with all speed.
